 Follow Texas lawmaker files bill to strengthen Lone Star Card security following millions in stolen SNAP benefits
 Daranesha Herron (KVUE) Tue, November 17, 2026 at 9:49 PM UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. KVUE A Texas lawmaker wants to strengthen security protections for families who rely on food assistance after a KVUE investigation revealed millions of dollars in stolen benefits and outdated technology that leaves recipients vulnerable to fraud.
 State Sen. Judith Zaffirini (D-Laredo) filed Senate Bill 374 on Nov. 13. The legislation would require electronic benefit transfer (EBT) cards used for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and the state's financial assistance programs to include security chips, similar to those commonly found in debit and credit cards.
 The proposal comes as nearly 40,000 Texas households have reported stolen benefits since May 2023, according to state data obtained by KVUE.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement A KVUE investigation found more than $21 million in SNAP benefits had been stolen from Texas families, highlighting a growing problem that has left some recipients struggling to afford groceries.
 Unlike most modern debit and credit cards, Texas Lone Star Cards still rely on magnetic stripes, making them vulnerable to a type of theft known as skimming.
 Criminals use hidden devices installed on card readers to capture card information. That information can then be copied onto fraudulent cards and used to drain recipients' accounts, sometimes within minutes of their benefits being deposited.
 RELATED: Weak EBT card security leaves millions in Texas SNAP benefits exposed to theft, $21M already stolen 
 Families left without food assistance
 In March, KVUE spoke with Austin resident Esmeralda Morales, whose entire $497 monthly SNAP benefit was stolen.
 Advertisement Advertisement The fraudulent transactions happened at stores in New Jersey, more than 1,600 miles from her home.
 Morales, who helps support six family members, said she was forced to take out a $200 loan and find additional work to put food on the table.
 "I was just upset. I was crying," Morales told KVUE. "I was thinking about, 'How am I going to get groceries for the two weeks, three weeks that they last?'"
 For families like Morales', recovering stolen benefits has become even more difficult. Federal authorization to reimburse SNAP benefits stolen through skimming and similar fraud expired for thefts occurring after Dec. 20, 2024.
 Advertisement Advertisement KVUE's investigation found more than $6.7 million in reimbursement claims filed in Texas in 2025 went unpaid.
 A proposed solution to an ongoing problem
 SB 374 would require Texas to transition to chip-enabled EBT cards, allowing recipients to insert or tap their cards instead of relying solely on magnetic stripes.
 Experts say the technology would make it significantly harder for criminals to duplicate stolen card information.
 During KVUE's investigation, Adam Colby, chief investigator at the Texas Financial Crimes Intelligence Center, said switching to chip technology should be a priority.
 "Simply placing the chip on there is going to slow the process down and makes the whole system much less vulnerable," Colby said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Colby acknowledged that replacing existing cards would come at a cost, but said lawmakers should consider that expense against the millions of dollars already lost to fraud.
 The potential solution isn't new. A 2023 report from the Texas Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General recommended transitioning to chip-enabled EBT cards. However, Texas has continued issuing cards without that technology.
 In a written statement to KVUE, Zaffirini said families should not have to worry about criminals stealing the benefits they need to buy groceries.
 "SNAP recipients should have the same protections against electronic theft that consumers have come to expect from their credit and debit cards," Zaffirini wrote.
 Advertisement Advertisement She also expressed optimism that the legislation could receive support from both political parties.
 "I am optimistic that SB 374 can attract bipartisan support because protecting families from fraud and safeguarding taxpayer dollars are priorities for many legislators," she wrote.
 How much would the upgrade cost?
 The cost of transitioning Texas' EBT system to chip technology has not yet been determined.
 Zaffirini said the Legislative Budget Board would prepare a fiscal note estimating expenses associated with replacing cards, updating payment systems and coordinating with retailers as the bill moves through the legislative process. She said lawmakers should also consider the potential long-term savings associated with preventing fraud.
 Advertisement Advertisement Although the proposed legislation focuses on preventing future theft, it does not establish a reimbursement program for families whose benefits have already been stolen.
 Zaffirini acknowledged those families still need help.
 "Families whose SNAP benefits have been stolen should not be left without the resources necessary to purchase food," she wrote.
 SB 374 was filed ahead of the 2027 legislative session, which begins in January. It would need approval from both chambers and the governor's signature to become law.
 KVUE previously investigated how criminals are stealing SNAP benefits, the organized networks behind the thefts and the financial hardship families face when their benefits disappear. Read the full investigation for a closer look at the security gaps in Texas' Lone Star Card system and what experts say could help prevent future theft.
